claims.text: Traditional full-fusion repair of the target component has a high risk of hot cracking because of its microstructure and melting behavior.
An HEA-based layer can be deposited by laser cladding as a repair or wear-resistant coating.
Laser cladding has lower overall thermal input and shorter exposure in the melting range than traditional fusion-welding repair.
The lower thermal exposure of laser cladding will prevent the hot cracking produced by traditional fusion welding.
Rapid, controlled laser deposition minimizes heat input.
Laser cladding produces a fine, crack-resistant repair-zone microstructure.
The repair will use a low- to moderate-power laser in an inert atmosphere.
The cladded layer will be metallurgically bonded to the component.
The repair will have a refined microstructure and a minimized heat-affected zone.
A refined microstructure and minimized heat-affected zone will prevent segregation and low-melting phases responsible for hot cracking.
Rapid solidification during laser cladding reduces time at temperatures where low-melting phases form.
Tailoring the HEA composition to avoid deleterious phases suppresses hot cracking.
The resulting repair layer will maintain mechanical integrity under high-stress and high-temperature service.
The laser-clad repair will exhibit significantly less hot cracking than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-clad repair will have greater toughness than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-clad repair will have greater wear resistance than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
The laser-clad repair will have better overall mechanical performance than a traditional fusion-welded repair.
HEA coatings have previously shown improved hardness, wear performance, or component service life.
The intervention is applicable under the component's typical operating temperatures and mechanical loads, provided the substrate remains within verified phase-stability limits.
Optimal laser parameters, the specific HEA composition, and long-term cyclic reliability remain experimentally undetermined.
